title: Three perfect days in Las Vegas: bulls, Boulder City and the Fugees' Score
dek: The SEMA Show opens its doors to the public, the PBR crowns its team champions on the Strip, and Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean play The Score at 30. Fit in a morning at Hoover Dam between the shows.

hero.wiki: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
hero.caption: The Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign at the south end of the Strip, where this weekend's drive out to Hoover Dam begins.

intro:
Las Vegas does not do quiet weekends, but this one has an unusual mix. On Friday the **SEMA Show**, the giant trade show of custom cars and aftermarket parts, opens to the general public for its last day at the Las Vegas Convention Center. That evening the **PBR Team Series Championship** begins three nights of bull riding at T-Mobile Arena, and at Resorts World, **Ms. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean** play a one-night celebration of *The Score*, the Fugees album that turns 30 this year. Tim McGraw is at the Colosseum on Friday and Saturday, *The Book of Mormon* is in the middle of a short run at The Venetian, and Santana plays a small room at House of Blues on Saturday.

Daylight saving time ended last Sunday, so the sun now sets around 5 p.m. That suits the city: the Strip is at its best after dark, and the desert is at its best in the morning. So this plan puts the long walks early. Saturday starts in Boulder City with coffee, a tour inside Hoover Dam and a flat trail through old railroad tunnels above Lake Mead, then comes back to town for northern Thai food at the reopened original Lotus of Siam and a late *O* at Bellagio.

Friday stays on the north end of the Strip, from the Peppermill to the canals of The Venetian, and Sunday goes off-Strip to the Arts District and Springs Preserve before the PBR final and the Bellagio fountains. The Raiders play away in Santa Clara on Sunday and the Golden Knights have no home game, so Allegiant Stadium is quiet and the crowds belong to cowboys and car people.

days.title: Friday: the north Strip, from hot rods to The Score
days.intro: A day that stays between the Convention Center and Resorts World: breakfast at a Strip landmark, the one public day of the SEMA Show, a gondola, Peking duck and a reunion of two Fugees.

stops.name: Peppermill Restaurant & Fireside Lounge
stops.text: The neon-and-mirrors coffee shop has been on the Strip since 1972, appeared in *Casino*, and won a James Beard America's Classics award in 2024. Breakfast is the meal to have here: the big fresh fruit salad, or the French toast ambrosia if you want to be fed until dinner. Afterward, look into the Fireside Lounge next door: it is where you come back for tiki drinks in 64-ounce fishbowls if the night goes long. It is a short walk or ride from the Convention Center.

stops.name: SEMA Show public day
stops.text: For most of the week the SEMA Show is trade-only, but Friday, November 6, is the one day the general public can walk the halls of custom builds, restored classics, off-road rigs and the newest aftermarket parts. Doors are open 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Friday, closing an hour earlier than the rest of the week, so give it the late morning and keep comfortable shoes on: the show fills the Convention Center. The Monorail stops at the Convention Center and is running extended hours for the show.

stops.name: Redhead Burger
stops.text: A Miami Beach smash-burger counter that opened its first West Coast location inside the Grand Canal Shoppes in May. The menu is short and to the point: smash burgers, fresh-cut fries, tater tots and milkshakes. It is a quick, inexpensive lunch after a morning on your feet, and it puts you a few steps from the gondola landing for the afternoon. It is open daily from 11 a.m.

stops.name: Gondola ride at The Venetian
stops.text: Yes, it is a gondola in a shopping mall, and that is the joy of it: a singing gondolier poles you along an indoor canal under a painted Venetian sky for 10 to 13 minutes. Buy tickets at Emporio d'Gondola on Level 2 of the Grand Canal Shoppes; shared boats take up to four people, and The Venetian lists lower prices on select November dates. On a clear afternoon the outdoor ride on the lagoon by the Strip is the other choice, with the ticket booth near the Doge's Palace entrance.

stops.name: Mott 32
stops.text: The Hong Kong restaurant's first American restaurant opened here at The Palazzo, and the reason to come is the Peking duck, along with dim sum and dishes from Cantonese, Szechuan and Beijing cooking. Order the duck when you sit down and build the rest of the meal around it with a few dim sum plates. Book ahead, especially on a big concert night, and eat early: the show at Resorts World starts at 8 p.m., a short ride up the Strip.

stops.name: Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean
stops.text: The two founding members of the Fugees perform the music of *The Score* for its 30th anniversary, for one night only in Las Vegas. The album gave the world "Killing Me Softly" and "Ready or Not," and this is a theater show, not an arena one. Tickets sell through AXS. If the night still has legs afterward, the Peppermill's Fireside Lounge is a short ride back down the Strip.

days.title: Saturday: Hoover Dam and Boulder City, then Thai food and O
days.intro: Rent a car or book a ride for the morning: the desert is cool and clear early, Hoover Dam's tours sell out, and the city's best Thai restaurant and its best water show wait back in town.

stops.name: Dam Roast House & Browder Bookstore
stops.text: Boulder City was built to house the workers on Hoover Dam, and its small historic downtown is the right place to start the day. This coffee house opens at 6 a.m. and pours locally sourced coffee drinks with fresh food to go with them, and it shares the space with a bookstore, so you can pick up something to read while your order comes. Take the coffee for a walk along Nevada Way before driving the last few miles to the dam.

stops.name: Hoover Dam
stops.text: Be at the visitor center when it opens at 9 a.m. The Guided Dam Tour, which takes you through the historic tunnels, up to the top of the dam and into the powerplant, is sold only on site, first come, first served, and it routinely sells out. The Power Plant Tour and the self-guided visitor center can be booked online. Park in the Nevada-side garage for $10, or free on the Arizona side if you do not mind the walk. Firearms, drones and similar items are not allowed on the dam.

stops.name: Historic Railroad Trail
stops.text: A flat, hard-packed gravel trail along the old railroad bed that carried materials to the dam, with five tunnels about 25 feet wide cut through the rock and long views over Lake Mead. The whole trail is 3.7 miles each way; walk out as far as the tunnels and turn back when you like. Park below the Lake Mead Visitor Center on Lakeshore Road. It is in a national park fee area, so keep your pass or receipt in the car. There is little shade, so carry water even in November.

stops.name: The Dillinger
stops.text: Back in Boulder City, this burger-and-craft-beer bar has been feeding locals since 2011. Order the Prime Rib Melt, which the Review-Journal's guide to the town singles out, and something cold from the tap list. Afterward walk a block or two: the town's public art program has put about 30 sculptures along its main streets, and Boulder Dam Brewing on Nevada Way pours six beers it brews on site if someone else is driving.

stops.name: Lotus of Siam
stops.text: Saipin Chutima opened Lotus of Siam in a strip mall in 1999 and built a following, Anthony Bourdain and Jonathan Gold among it, for her northern Thai cooking. The original Sahara Avenue restaurant closed in 2021 and reopened this June with throwback dishes, a new cocktail bar called Naam Jai and a 6,000-bottle wine cellar. Order from the northern Thai side of the menu and ask for help with the wine. Dinner runs Wednesday to Sunday, 5 to 10 p.m.; book ahead.

stops.name: O by Cirque du Soleil
stops.text: Cirque du Soleil's water show has run at Bellagio since 1998, and it is still the one to see if you see one: divers, swimmers and acrobats perform on, above and under a stage that turns into a pool and back again. Saturday has two performances, at 6:30 and 9 p.m.; the later one gives you time for dinner. Buy tickets ahead for a Saturday.

days.title: Sunday: the Arts District, the springs and the bulls
days.intro: A slower morning off the Strip, where Las Vegas began at a desert spring, then back to the south-center Strip for the PBR final, Korean tacos and the fountains.

stops.name: Makers & Finders
stops.text: A coffee house and brunch spot with Latin American cooking and several locations around the valley, including this one on Main Street. Come for coffee and a plate from the brunch menu, which has run to empanadas and lomo saltado. Weekend mornings are busy and parking on Main Street is tight, so arrive early or come by ride-share. After breakfast, take a slow walk along Main Street before the short drive to Springs Preserve.

stops.name: Springs Preserve
stops.text: The city grew up around the springs on this site, and the preserve tells the story: botanical gardens of desert plants, a wetland trail, the Nevada State Museum and galleries, and a train that tours the grounds. It is open seven days a week, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. in fall and winter, and gardens and trails close at 4 p.m. or dusk, whichever comes first. Give it two hours, start with the gardens while the light is good, and eat at the Springs Cafe if you need lunch.

stops.name: PBR Team Series Championship final
stops.text: The championship weekend ends on Sunday afternoon with the final. PBR's team format is easy to follow even if you have never seen bull riding: five riders from one franchise face five from another, and the higher combined score advances. Single-day tickets sell through AXS and the T-Mobile Arena box office. The arena's bag policy allows only small clutches, so travel light, and walk in through the Park between New York-New York and Park MGM.

stops.name: Best Friend
stops.text: Roy Choi's Korean-Los Angeles restaurant has been at Park MGM since 2018, and it is a few steps from the arena. Share a table's worth: the banchan sampler, Korean wings, kimchi fried rice and the Kogi short rib tacos from Choi's food-truck days. The main room plays loud and feels like a party; ask about the chef's table inside the kitchen for something calmer. It opens at 4 p.m. and runs to 11 p.m. on Sundays. Book ahead after the bull riding lets out.

stops.name: Fountains of Bellagio
stops.text: End the weekend with the free show the whole Strip stops for. From 8 p.m. the fountains dance every 15 minutes until midnight, so walk up the Strip from Park MGM after dinner and you will not wait long. For a side-on view of the whole lake, stand on the pedestrian bridge by The Cosmopolitan; for a lower and quieter one, try the low stone wall by Bellagio's valet. The show pauses when the wind is over 20 mph.

stay.name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas
stay.text: A hotel without a casino in the middle of the Strip, which is the point: the rooms are calm, and you are a short walk from Bellagio, Park MGM and T-Mobile Arena for Saturday night at *O* and Sunday's PBR final and fountains.

stay.name: The Venetian Resort
stay.text: The Strip's version of Venice, with the canals, the gondolas and Mott 32 under one roof, and suites as standard rooms. Friday's whole day is within walking distance or a short ride, from the Convention Center to Resorts World, and *The Book of Mormon* is in its theater this weekend.

stay.name: Park MGM
stay.text: A mid-priced, smoke-free resort next to T-Mobile Arena, with Best Friend downstairs and the walk through the Park to the arena right outside. It is the easiest base for PBR weekend, and Bellagio and its fountains are a short walk north.

events.name: SEMA Show public day
events.text: The trade show of custom cars, trucks and aftermarket parts runs Nov. 3 to 6, and Friday is the only day it is open to the general public. Expect heavy traffic around Paradise Road all week.

events.name: PBR Team Series Championship
events.when: Fri. Nov. 6 to Sun. Nov. 8; Friday's first bull at about 7:45 p.m.
events.text: The season's team bull-riding title is decided over three days of 5-on-5 matchups, ending with Sunday afternoon's final. Single-day tickets and three-day passes sell through AXS.

events.name: Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean: The Score at 30
events.text: The Fugees' founding members celebrate the 30th anniversary of *The Score* in a one-night Las Vegas show. Tickets on AXS.

events.name: Tim McGraw
events.text: The last two of the country star's five fall shows at the Colosseum.

events.name: The Book of Mormon
events.when: Through Nov. 15; Fri. 7:30 p.m., Sat. 2 and 7:30 p.m.
events.text: The touring production of the Tony-winning musical plays a limited run at The Venetian from Nov. 4 to 15.

events.name: An Intimate Evening with Santana
events.text: SiriusXM presents an intimate evening with the guitarist Carlos Santana at the House of Blues.

events.name: Brad Paisley: One Man, Six Strings
events.where: Encore Theater at Wynn Las Vegas
events.text: The country guitarist plays a pared-down show in the Encore Theater.

know: **From the airport.** Harry Reid International (LAS) sits just south of the Strip. Taxis wait outside baggage claim at both terminals and charge flat zone fares to the Strip: $21.25 to hotels south of Tropicana Avenue, $25.25 from Tropicana to Flamingo Road and $29.25 from Flamingo north to The STRAT, plus a card fee where it applies. Uber and Lyft pick up on Level 2 of the Terminal 1 garage and on the valet level of the Terminal 3 garage.

**Getting around.** The Deuce bus runs the length of the Strip to downtown 24 hours a day: $4 a ride, $8 for 24 hours or $20 for three days, paid in the rideRTC app, at machines or by tapping a contactless card. The Monorail runs behind the east side of the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA, with a stop at the Convention Center, and stays open until 3 a.m. on Friday for the SEMA Show.

**Saturday needs a car.** Hoover Dam and Boulder City are southeast of the city and not served by Strip transit; rent a car for the day or book a tour. At the dam, the Guided Dam Tour is sold only on site, and parking is $10 in the Nevada garage or free in Arizona-side lots 13 and 14.

**SEMA traffic.** The SEMA Show fills the Convention Center through Friday afternoon, so expect slow traffic around Paradise Road and the north Strip, and use the Monorail to the Convention Center stop if you are going.
**Early sunsets.** Daylight saving time ended on Nov. 1, so the sun sets around 5 p.m. Plan outdoor walks for the morning and carry a layer for the evening.
**Tipping.** Tip as you would anywhere in the United States: 18 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants, a dollar or two a drink at the bar, and something for housekeeping, valets and bell staff.
**Bag policies.** T-Mobile Arena allows only small clutches or wallets, no backpacks or large purses, so leave big bags at the hotel.
